text:
incident-bot: PAGE: high error-rate for runtime-fallbacks-prod (alerts/prometheus/runtime_fallbacks_error_rate > 5% for 5m)
Mateo: I’m on it, pinging SREs and checking the runtime dashboard.
Erin: I see a spike in fallback count and a matching increase in KV cache evictions. Could be cache churn causing timeouts.
Mateo: Any customer-facing errors reported? Priya, are we seeing support tickets?
Priya: No new tickets yet, but some telemetry shows increased 5xx responses to the hosted inference API starting ~12:03 UTC. Small percentage but correlates with fallbacks.
Josh: I’m rolling up logs from the runtime nodes now. If it’s KV pressure, we might need to increase cache size or temporarily route traffic to next-best model variant.
Li: Noted. Routing policy can fallback to model-variant v2-quant with lower memory needs. Want me to flip it?
Mateo: Yes, prepare the policy. Erin, can you verify drop-in compatibility for v2-quant?
Erin: v2-quant is compatible, but outputs differ slightly — we need to mark degraded-quality for customers and only route non-critical routes.
Mateo: Ok plan: 1) Create a 30m maintenance window to silence noisy runtime_fallbacks alert 2) Route non-SLA traffic to v2-quant 3) Increase KV cache TTL on-hot path by 50% as temp mitigation 4) Observe for 15m then decide rollback or permanent config change
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged by Mateo (oncall).
Mateo: @Li please apply routing change with a canary of 10% first. Add logging tag runtime-mitigation-183999 for tracing.
Li: applying canary now. CLI: ```sh
redwoodctl route apply --policy runtime-fallbacks-mitigation --canary 10 --tag runtime-mitigation-183999
```
Li: canary 10% live, no immediate errors in canary logs.
Erin: I’ve bumped KV cache TTL on the serving pool: ```yaml
- param: kv_cache_ttl
  old: 120s
  new: 180s
```
Erin: watching eviction metrics... eviction-rate trending downwards after ~90s.
Josh: logs show a subset of nodes with repeated OOM-ish behavior at ~12:05 — those nodes were on model-variant v3-large. Canary avoids sending to that fleet.
Mateo: Good, start a 30-minute silence on the runtime_fallbacks alert so it doesn’t page on noise while we validate. Command: ```bash
opsctl silence create --alert runtime_fallbacks_error_rate --duration 30m --reason "mitigation in progress - validating kv ttl and canary"
```
Mateo: done. Silence created.
Erin: Dashboard check: latency p50/p95 are stable, p99 improved on the canary path. Overall fallback rate down from 7.2% to 2.1% over 10 minutes.
Priya: Customer-impact summary for support: small percentage of requests (estimated 1.8%) experienced degraded response or model-variant differences; no major customers reported. I’ll draft a short internal note and keep support on standby.
Josh: Suggestion post-incident: we should add a dashboard panel that breaks fallback rate down by model-variant and by KV eviction rate side-by-side. Current dashboards are too aggregated.
Mateo: Agreed — include per-region too. Add as action item.
Li: Canary at 30% now, still stable. If metrics hold for another 10m we can promote to 100% for non-SLA traffic and consider upgrading cache permanently.
Erin: Running a quick validate of alert thresholds — current alert fires on >5% for 5m. Given typical transient skews, propose new threshold >6% for 10m with alerting to pager only if customer 5xxs >0.5% simultaneously.
Mateo: Make that a proposal PR to monitoring repo so we have history. Also add runbook note linking to the routing policy to avoid reflex silences.
Li: I’ll open the PR: https://git.internal/redwood/monitoring/pull/487 (draft) — includes proposed threshold change and a dashboard link.
Erin: Can we also add an automated validation job that compares fallback rate against KV eviction delta before firing severe alerts?
Mateo: Good idea. Add to backlog and mark as P1 for the next on-call retro.
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: On-call handoff scheduled in 45m.
Priya: Support note ready, will post to #customer-impact and notify any customers who ping.
Mateo: Transition plan: I’ll remain primary until next handoff, then update the oncall with the mitigation steps and the PR link. Final state for handoff: canary at 30%, KV TTL +50%, silence in place until 12:40 UTC.
Erin: I’ll monitor for the next 20m and start drafting the post-incident alert-cleanup checklist: silences to remove after validation, maintenance windows to create for future deploys, and the new per-variant panels.
Josh: Also capture the node fleet that exhibited OOM signs for a deeper postmortem — maybe model packing/placement issue.
Mateo: Thanks team. If metrics bounce back we’ll revert the routing. Otherwise we’ll convert the mitigations to a follow-up change with a controlled rollout.
Erin: Quick thumbs: :thumbsup:
Li: :eyes: will follow the PR.
Mateo: Closing this thread when the 30m silence ends and we have final validation. For now, paging suppressed and mitigation holding.
